source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
In more developed/mechanized regions, drying is done using drying equipment: to dry ears, a drying chamber/machine is set at a temperature of about 40-45 degrees Celsius, applied after the ears have already partially dried in the field (with kernel moisture at about 17-20%). The ears are then fed into a sheller machine, and kernels are placed into a drying bin/room and dried further until kernel moisture reaches about 18-19%.

Where sun-drying is used instead: after field-drying, ears are shelled by machine and the kernels are then spread out to dry in the sun until moisture content reaches about 18-19%.

Once kernel moisture is brought down to the range of about 18-19%, the grain can be stored in sacks for a relatively short period, but if stored for a longer duration the moisture must be reduced further, to a range of about 14-15%, since if moisture is too high the grain is prone to mold growth.

When drying by machine, care should be taken regarding the seed's germ (embryo), so that heat exposure does not damage seed intended for planting -- seed should not be scorched, cracked, or broken, and should be handled to avoid excessive impact damage that could harm the embryo inside the dryer.

Regarding mechanical harvesting (combine harvesting), the source notes that harvesting by machine works best/most efficiently when kernel moisture content is at about 25% at the time of harvest.
